claims.text: Lint passes on src, tests and evals.
The full suite passes with no skips.

Contracts tier: a SQLite checkpoint written by the actual previous release's `cma run` (cba9dba source extracted with git archive, run in a child interpreter that asserts it imported that tree) holds Transactions with only the seven old fields, and this release's `cma resume` approves it, writing a memo stamped 'APPROVED by C. Later' and evidence with schema_version 1. The previous release's own Transaction model loads a line this one writes. All extras (anthropic, openai, mcp, langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite) import. Today's evidence keys are a subset of the new record. Two runs give equal key sets, and a replay onto an existing --out exits 2 and leaves the memo and evidence byte-identical.

claims.text: Dual-run tier: on every synthetic archetype and profile and on the committed example, M1-M16 have the same ids, units, values and evidence under cba9dba and T02. Only M2's method sentence differs.
The offline evals still ground every memo.

dispositions.finding: major tests/test_models.py:205: the SQLite contract resumes a simulated old payload created by the current CLI, not a checkpoint written by the old version.
dispositions.evidence: Added tests/test_previous_release.py::test_a_checkpoint_written_by_the_previous_release_resumes (contracts). It extracts cba9dba's src with git archive (tests/previous_release.py) and runs the old `cma run --checkpoint-db ... --thread t02-legacy` in a child process with EOF at the prompt. It decodes the stored blobs to check that every stored Transaction has exactly the old seven fields, then runs T02's `cma resume t02-legacy --reviewer 'C. Later' --out ...`, answers y, and checks the APPROVED memo and schema_version 1 in its evidence. test_the_previous_release_is_really_the_old_code proves the child imports the old tree (13 categories, no new fields). Both pass in the contracts tier.

dispositions.evidence: Added contracts test test_all_extras_are_installed, which imports anthropic, openai, mcp and langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite and fails if any is missing. It passes in the contracts tier.

dispositions.finding: minor tests/test_models.py:283: idempotency claim cites a single run; no replay or key-set equality proof.
dispositions.evidence: Added contracts test test_a_second_run_with_the_same_out_is_refused_and_leaves_the_record: two runs to separate --out paths give equal evidence key sets, and a third run onto the first --out exits 2 with 'Refusing to overwrite' and leaves the memo and evidence byte-for-byte unchanged. It passes.

dispositions.finding: minor tests/test_models.py:311: rollback contract uses a local _PreviousTransaction, not the actual previous release's model.
dispositions.evidence: Added contracts test test_the_previous_release_loads_a_transaction_this_one_writes: a T02 Transaction with the three new fields is validated by cba9dba's own cma.models.Transaction in a child process, and the result equals the original minus the new fields. It passes.

dispositions.finding: minor src/cma/metrics.py:252: no proof committed values are unchanged (dual_run selected zero tests); timing claim unproven.
dispositions.evidence: Added dual_run tests test_m1_to_m16_are_unchanged_from_the_previous_release (every synth archetype x profile) and test_the_committed_example_is_unchanged_from_the_previous_release. They compare id, unit, value and evidence for every metric between cba9dba (child process) and T02, and assert that only M2's method text differs. The dual_run tier now selects 10 tests, all passing. The timing claim is withdrawn and not made here.

notes: The previous-release tests need git and BASE (cba9dbad600f3258de587780dd6e3a46ff59203a) in the repository's object store, which this worktree has. Without them they fail rather than skip. The older simulated-payload tests in tests/test_models.py are kept as extra coverage, but the claim rests on the real-release tests. No timing or wheel-install claim is made.
